title: What is Arun doing in Lucknow?
titleHi: अरुण जी लखनऊ में क्या कर रहे हैं ?
scope: The present and past continuous (बोल रहा है, बोल रही थीं), including near-future and phone use; “to have” with को (ailments), के पास (things, money, time) and का/की/के (relatives, houses, body parts); oblique adverbial phrases (पिछले साल, उन दिनों, सवेरे, तीसरे पहर) and oblique destinations (कलकत्ते जाना); adverbs with से and पर (ज़ोर से, अच्छी तरह, आम तौर पर); postposition parts as adverbs (ऊपर, बाहर); कैसे, सीधे; dates (पहली, दूसरी, then cardinals; सन्); word order and emphasis; colloquial usage and minimal pairs

vocab.en: to live a life of pleasure
to come out, go out, emerge

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother is making tea in the kitchen.”
items.hi: माँ रसोईघर में चाय बना ___ हैं ।
items.say: माँ रसोईघर में चाय बना रही हैं ।
items.en: Mother[0] {is making}[4+5+6] tea[3] in[2] the kitchen[1].
wrong: रहा
रहा is masculine. माँ is a woman: बना रही हैं.
रहे
रहे is masculine plural. Respect makes a woman's auxiliary plural (हैं), but रही stays feminine.
items.why: रहा, रही, रहे agree with the subject like an -ā adjective; the auxiliary comes last.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children are playing in the garden.”
items.hi: बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेल रहे ___ ।
items.say: बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेल रहे हैं ।
wrong: है
है is singular. बच्चे is plural: खेल रहे हैं.
हो
हो goes only with तुम.
items.why: The auxiliary is the present of होना, agreeing with the subject: हूँ, है, हैं, हो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What are you thinking? (to a man)”
items.hi: तुम क्या सोच ___ हो ?
items.say: तुम क्या सोच रहे हो ?
items.en: What[1] are[4] you[0] thinking[2+3]? (to a man)
wrong: रहा
रहा is singular. तुम always takes plural agreement: सोच रहे हो.
रहते
रहते is the imperfective participle of रहना “to live, stay”. The continuous needs रहा, रही or रहे straight after the stem.
items.why: To a woman: तुम क्या सोच रही हो ?

items.q: Make it continuous (“is …ing”)
items.a: राज अपनी साइकिल धो रहा है ।
wrong: राज अपनी साइकिल धोना रहा है ।
The continuous is built on the stem धो, not on the infinitive धोना.
राज अपनी साइकिल धो रहा हैं ।
हैं is plural. Raj, spoken of plainly, takes है.
items.why: Replace the participle धोता with the stem + रहा — धो रहा है.
items.hi: राज अपनी साइकिल धोता है ।
items.say: राज अपनी साइकिल धो रहा है ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am writing stories for the children. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं बच्चों के लिए ___ लिख रहा हूँ ।
items.say: मैं बच्चों के लिए कहानियाँ लिख रहा हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {am writing}[5+6+7] stories[4] for[2+3] the children[1]. (a man speaking)
wrong: कहानी
कहानी is singular, “a story”. The English has “stories”.
कहानियें
Not a word: feminine nouns in -ī make the plural in -iyā̃, as in लड़कियाँ.
items.why: कहानी “story” is feminine: plural कहानियाँ.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Hello, is that Pinki speaking?”
items.hi: हलो, क्या पिंकी बोल ___ है ?
items.say: हलो, क्या पिंकी बोल रही है ?
wrong: रहा
रहा is masculine. Pinki is a girl.
रहे
रहे is plural. Pinki, spoken of plainly, takes the singular: बोल रही है.
items.why: On the phone the continuous identifies the speaker: मैं … बोल रहा हूँ (or रही हूँ) “this is … speaking”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What are you reading nowadays? (to a man)”
items.hi: आप आजकल क्या पढ़ ___ हैं ?
items.say: आप आजकल क्या पढ़ रहे हैं ?
items.en: What[2] are[5] you[0] reading[3+4] nowadays[1]? (to a man)
wrong: रहा
रहा is singular. आप always takes plural agreement: पढ़ रहे हैं.
रही
रही is feminine. This is asked of a man.
items.why: The continuous also covers what is going on over a period, like English “these days I'm reading …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We are going to Lucknow on Saturday.”
items.hi: हम लोग शनिवार को लखनऊ ___ रहे हैं ।
items.say: हम लोग शनिवार को लखनऊ जा रहे हैं ।
items.en: We[0+1] {are going}[5+6+7] to Lucknow[4] on Saturday[2+3].
wrong: जाना
The continuous is built on the stem: जा रहे हैं, not on the infinitive जाना.
जाओ
जाओ is the तुम command. The continuous needs the bare stem: जा रहे हैं.
items.why: The continuous can refer to a planned event in the near future, as English “we are going on Saturday”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Father is reading the newspaper.”
items.hi: पिता जी अख़बार पढ़ रहे ___ ।
items.say: पिता जी अख़बार पढ़ रहे हैं ।
wrong: है
A respected person takes plural agreement: पिता जी … पढ़ रहे हैं.
हूँ goes only with मैं.
items.why: Respect makes both रहे and the auxiliary plural.

items.q: Which means “Raj isn't working today”?
items.a: राज आज काम नहीं कर रहा है ।
wrong: राज आज काम नहीं करता है ।
करता है is the imperfective: “Raj doesn't work” as a habit. What is going on now needs the continuous, कर रहा है.
राज आज काम नहीं कर रही है ।
रही is feminine. Raj is a man.
items.why: नहीं goes before the verb: नहीं कर रहा है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “At ten o'clock last night I was reading a story. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: कल रात दस बजे मैं एक कहानी पढ़ ___ था ।
items.say: कल रात दस बजे मैं एक कहानी पढ़ रहा था ।
items.en: {At ten o'clock}[2+3] {last night}[0+1] I[4] {was reading}[7+8+9] a[5] story[6]. (a man speaking)
wrong: रही
रही is feminine. The speaker is a man.
रहे
रहे is plural. मैं takes the singular: पढ़ रहा था.
items.why: The past continuous is the stem + रहा, रही, रहे + था, थी, थे, थीं — “was …ing”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “At that time the girls were playing outside.”
items.hi: उस समय लड़कियाँ बाहर खेल रही ___ ।
items.say: उस समय लड़कियाँ बाहर खेल रही थीं ।
items.en: {At that time}[0+1] the girls[2] {were playing}[4+5+6] outside[3].
wrong: थी
थी is singular. लड़कियाँ is plural.
थे
थे is masculine. लड़कियाँ is feminine.
items.why: Feminine plural: रही थीं. Only the auxiliary carries the plural nasal.

items.q: Which means “The women were laughing”?
wrong: औरतें हँस रहीं थीं ।
With the auxiliary present only थीं carries the plural nasal: रही थीं, just as उठती थीं.
औरतें हँस रही थी ।
थी is singular. औरतें is plural: थीं.
items.why: रही is the same for feminine singular and plural; the auxiliary shows the number.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Last year my brothers were working in Lucknow.”
items.hi: पिछले साल मेरे भाई लखनऊ में काम कर रहे ___ ।
items.say: पिछले साल मेरे भाई लखनऊ में काम कर रहे थे ।
items.en: {Last year}[0+1] my[2] brothers[3] {were working}[6+7+8+9] in[5] Lucknow[4].
wrong: था
था is singular. The English has “brothers”, and रहे is plural: रहे थे.
थीं is feminine. भाई is masculine.
items.why: रहे थे “were …ing” for a masculine plural subject.

items.q: Put it in the past (“was …ing”)
items.a: सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ गपशप कर रही थी ।
wrong: सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ गपशप कर रहा था ।
रहा is masculine. Only the auxiliary changes: रही है becomes रही थी.
सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ गपशप करती थी ।
करती थी is the past imperfective, “used to chat”. “Was chatting” keeps रही.
items.why: Replace है with थी. रही stays.
items.hi: सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ गपशप कर रही है ।
items.say: सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ गपशप कर रही थी ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where were you going yesterday evening? (to a woman)”
items.hi: तुम कल शाम को कहाँ जा रही ___ ?
items.say: तुम कल शाम को कहाँ जा रही थीं ?
items.en: Where[4] {were you}[0+7] going[5+6] {yesterday evening}[1+2+3]? (to a woman)
wrong: थी
तुम always takes plural agreement: a woman is asked … जा रही थीं.
थे
थे is masculine. This is asked of a woman.
items.why: तुम with a woman: रही हो in the present, रही थीं in the past.

lessons.title: मेरे पास, मेरी बहिन
lessons.desc: Saying “to have”: को, के पास, का

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita has three sisters.”
items.hi: सीता ___ तीन बहिनें हैं ।
items.say: सीता की तीन बहिनें हैं ।
wrong: का
का goes with a masculine singular noun. The possessive agrees with बहिनें, which is feminine: की.
को
को is used for ailments such as a cold or fever. For relatives, use का, की, के.
items.why: Relatives, houses and parts of the body: X का, की, के … है, agreeing with what is possessed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My uncle has a big house in the village.”
items.hi: मेरे चाचा जी ___ गाँव में एक बड़ा मकान है ।
items.say: मेरे चाचा जी का गाँव में एक बड़ा मकान है ।
items.en: My[0] uncle[1+2] has[3+9] a[6] big[7] house[8] in[5] the village[4].
wrong: की
की is feminine. The possessive agrees with मकान, which is masculine: का.
को
को is for ailments. For a house, use का, की, के.
items.why: The possessive agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner: चाचा जी का मकान.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Do you have a car?”
items.say: क्या आपके पास गाड़ी है ?
wrong: आपका
Before पास the possessive is oblique: आपके पास.
आप
के पास needs the possessive before it: आपके पास.
items.why: Portable things, money and time: X के पास … है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My husband has had a fever since yesterday.”
items.hi: मेरे पति ___ कल से बुख़ार है ।
items.say: मेरे पति को कल से बुख़ार है ।
items.en: My[0] husband[1+2] {has had}[6] a fever[5] since[4] yesterday[3].
wrong: का
का, की, के are for relatives, houses and parts of the body. Ailments take को.
की
की is for relatives and the like, and बुख़ार is masculine anyway. Ailments take को.
items.why: Ailments: X को बुख़ार है, X को ज़ुकाम है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “That woman has four sons.”
items.hi: उस औरत ___ चार बेटे हैं ।
items.say: उस औरत के चार बेटे हैं ।
wrong: की
The possessive agrees with बेटे (masculine plural), not with the woman: के.
को
को is for ailments. For relatives, use का, की, के.
items.why: Relatives, houses and parts of the body: X का, की, के … है, agreeing with what is possessed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have a younger sister.”
items.hi: ___ एक छोटी बहिन है ।
items.say: मेरी एक छोटी बहिन है ।
wrong: मेरे पास
के पास is for portable things, money and time. For a relative, use the possessive: मेरी.
मेरा
मेरा is masculine. It agrees with बहिन, which is feminine: मेरी.
items.why: With pronouns the possessive (मेरा, तुम्हारा …) stands in for X का — मेरी एक बहिन है “I have a sister”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have only two hours.”
items.hi: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ दो ___ हैं ।
items.say: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ दो घंटे हैं ।
wrong: घंटा
घंटा is singular. With दो it is plural: घंटे.
घंटें
Not a word: masculine nouns in -ā make the plural in -e, with no nasal.
items.why: Time is possessed with के पास — मेरे पास समय है.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This statue has four hands.”
items.hi: इस मूर्ति के चार ___ हैं ।
items.say: इस मूर्ति के चार हाथ हैं ।
wrong: हाथें
Not a word: masculine nouns that don't end in -ā are the same in the plural: चार हाथ.
हाथों
हाथों is the oblique plural, used before a postposition. Here the hands are the subject.
items.why: Parts of the body: के agrees with हाथ (masculine plural), whatever the gender of मूर्ति.

items.q: Put it in the past
items.a: मेरे पास एक पुरानी गाड़ी थी ।
wrong: मेरे पास एक पुरानी गाड़ी था ।
The verb agrees with गाड़ी, which is feminine: थी.
मेरी पास एक पुरानी गाड़ी थी ।
के पास never changes: मेरे पास, whatever is possessed.
items.why: In the के पास construction the thing possessed is the subject.
items.hi: मेरे पास एक पुरानी गाड़ी है ।
items.say: मेरे पास एक पुरानी गाड़ी थी ।

items.q: Which means “Do you have a pen?” (to तुम)
wrong: क्या तुम्हें क़लम है ?
The को construction (तुम्हें = तुम को) is for ailments. A pen is a portable thing: के पास.
क्या तुम्हारी पास क़लम है ?
के पास never changes, whatever is possessed: तुम्हारे पास.
items.why: Portable things, money and time: X के पास … है.

lessons.title: पिछले साल, उन दिनों
lessons.desc: Oblique phrases of time and place

items.q: Fill the gap: “Last year we were in London.”
items.hi: ___ साल हम लंदन में थे ।
items.say: पिछले साल हम लंदन में थे ।
wrong: पिछला
The phrase is oblique: पिछले साल.
अगले
अगले साल means “next year”.
पिछलें
Not a word: the oblique of पिछला is पिछले, with no nasal.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “My friends are coming from London next month.”
items.hi: अगले ___ मेरे दोस्त लंदन से आ रहे हैं ।
items.say: अगले महीने मेरे दोस्त लंदन से आ रहे हैं ।
items.en: My[2] friends[3] {are coming}[6+7+8] from[5] London[4] next[0] month[1].
wrong: महीना
The time phrase is oblique, so महीना becomes महीने.
महीनें
Not a word: the oblique of महीना is महीने, with no nasal.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “I get up early in the morning. (a man speaking)”
items.say: मैं सवेरे उठता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {get up}[2+3] {early in the morning}[1]. (a man speaking)
wrong: सवेरा
सवेरा is the noun “early morning”. As an adverb it is oblique: सवेरे.
सवेरें
Not a word: the oblique of सवेरा is सवेरे.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “In those days there was no electricity here.”
items.hi: उन ___ यहाँ बिजली नहीं थी ।
items.say: उन दिनों यहाँ बिजली नहीं थी ।
items.en: {In those days}[0+1] {there was}[5] no[4] electricity[3] here[2].
wrong: दिन
With उन the phrase is oblique plural: उन दिनों.
दिनें
Not a word: दिन has no plural in -ẽ. The oblique plural is दिनों.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “At what time do you go to the office?”
items.hi: आप ___ समय दफ़्तर जाते हैं ?
items.say: आप किस समय दफ़्तर जाते हैं ?
items.en: {At what}[1] time[2] do[5] you[0] go[4] {to the office}[3]?
wrong: कौन
कौन is direct. The phrase is oblique: किस समय.
क्या
क्या does not go before a noun to mean “which, what”. The oblique of कौन gives किस समय.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “My brother sleeps the whole day.”
items.hi: मेरा भाई ___ दिन सोता है ।
items.say: मेरा भाई सारे दिन सोता है ।
wrong: हर
हर दिन means “every day”. “The whole day” is सारे दिन, oblique.
सारी
सारी is feminine. दिन is masculine.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “I rest a little in the afternoon. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं ___ पहर थोड़ा आराम करता हूँ ।
items.say: मैं तीसरे पहर थोड़ा आराम करता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] rest[4+5+6] {a little}[3] {in the afternoon}[1+2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: तीसरा
The phrase is oblique: तीसरे पहर.
तीन
तीसरे पहर, “in the third watch”, is the afternoon. तीन पहर would be “three watches”.
items.why: Phrases of time like this are oblique even though no postposition follows (a “ghostposition”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “This evening we are going to the cinema.”
items.hi: ___ शाम हम सिनेमा जा रहे हैं ।
items.say: आज शाम हम सिनेमा जा रहे हैं ।
items.en: {This evening}[0+1] we[2] {are going}[4+5+6] to the cinema[3].
wrong: इस
“This evening” is आज शाम — इस and यह are not used here.
यह
“This evening” is आज शाम — यह and इस are not used here.
items.why: आज शाम “this evening”, आज सुबह “this morning”.

items.q: Why is it कलकत्ते in मेरे चाचा जी कलकत्ते जा रहे हैं ?
items.a: The destination of a verb of motion is usually oblique, as if a postposition were there
wrong: Because चाचा जी is plural
रहे हैं is plural for respect, but that has nothing to do with the place name.
Because the sentence is in the continuous
The tense makes no difference: वह कलकत्ते जाता है too.
items.why: Compare सीता अपने दफ़्तर जा रही है, where अपने shows the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan's house is in this direction.”
items.hi: मोहन का घर इस ___ है ।
items.say: मोहन का घर इस तरफ़ है ।
wrong: तरह
तरह means “way, manner”. “Direction” is तरफ़.
समय
समय means “time”.
items.why: इस तरफ़ “in this direction” is oblique, like the time phrases.

lessons.title: ज़ोर से, अच्छी तरह
lessons.desc: Adverbs with से and पर; ऊपर, सीधे, कैसे

items.q: Fill the gap: “He is speaking loudly.”
items.hi: वह ___ से बोल रहा है ।
items.say: वह ज़ोर से बोल रहा है ।
wrong: ध्यान
ध्यान से means “attentively”.
देर
देर से means “late”.
items.why: ज़ोर “force” + से = “forcefully, loudly”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We go to school by bus.”
items.hi: हम बस ___ स्कूल जाते हैं ।
items.say: हम बस से स्कूल जाते हैं ।
wrong: पर
Means of transport take से — बस से “by bus”.
का
का links two nouns (“the bus's …”). “By bus” is बस से.
items.why: से forms adverbial phrases: बस से, हाथ से, देर से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj always comes punctually.”
items.hi: राज हमेशा ___ समय पर आता है ।
items.say: राज हमेशा ठीक समय पर आता है ।
wrong: ग़ल्त
ग़ल्त समय पर would be “at the wrong time”.
किस
किस समय asks “at what time?”.
items.why: ठीक समय पर “punctually” is formed with पर.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita speaks Hindi very well.”
items.hi: सीता हिन्दी बहुत अच्छी ___ बोलती है ।
items.say: सीता हिन्दी बहुत अच्छी तरह बोलती है ।
wrong: तरफ़
तरफ़ means “direction”. “Well” is अच्छी तरह, “in a good manner”.
समय
अच्छा समय would be “a good time”. “Well” is अच्छी तरह.
items.why: अच्छी agrees with तरह (f); से may follow: अच्छी तरह से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Usually I drink tea in the morning. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: ___ तौर पर मैं सुबह चाय पीता हूँ ।
items.say: आम तौर पर मैं सुबह चाय पीता हूँ ।
items.en: Usually[0+1+2] I[3] drink[6+7] tea[5] {in the morning}[4]. (a man speaking)
wrong: ख़ास
ख़ास तौर पर means “specially”.
ठीक
ठीक goes with तरह or से, “properly”. “Usually” is आम तौर पर.
items.why: आम “ordinary” + तौर पर = “usually”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My office is upstairs.”
items.hi: मेरा दफ़्तर ___ है ।
items.say: मेरा दफ़्तर ऊपर है ।
wrong: नीचे
नीचे means “downstairs, below”.
के ऊपर
के ऊपर “on top of” needs a noun before it. On its own, ऊपर is an adverb: “upstairs”.
items.why: The second part of a compound postposition can stand alone as an adverb: ऊपर, नीचे, बाहर, अंदर.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please go straight.”
items.hi: आप ___ जाइए ।
items.say: आप सीधे जाइए ।
wrong: सीधी
सीधी is the feminine adjective “straight”. The adverb ends in -e: सीधे.
सीधें
Not a word: the adverb is सीधे, with no nasal.
items.why: Some adverbs in -e pair with adjectives: कैसा and कैसे, सीधा and सीधे, बायाँ and बायें.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How do you go to the office?”
items.hi: आप दफ़्तर ___ जाते हैं ?
items.say: आप दफ़्तर कैसे जाते हैं ?
items.en: How[2] do[4] you[0] go[3] {to the office}[1]?
wrong: कैसा
कैसा is the adjective “what kind of?”. “How?” is the adverb कैसे.
कैसी
कैसी is the feminine adjective. “How?” is the adverb कैसे.
items.why: कैसे “how?” does not change.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please drive the car carefully.”
items.hi: आप ___ से गाड़ी चलाइए ।
items.say: आप सावधानी से गाड़ी चलाइए ।
wrong: ज़ोर
ज़ोर से means “forcefully”.
देर
देर से means “late”.
items.why: सावधानी “care” + से = “carefully”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My daughter is coming on the first of March.”
items.hi: मेरी बेटी ___ मार्च को आ रही है ।
items.say: मेरी बेटी पहली मार्च को आ रही है ।
items.en: My[0] daughter[1] {is coming}[5+6+7] on[4] {the first}[2] of March[3].
wrong: पहला
पहला is masculine. A date agrees with the understood feminine तारीख़ “date”: पहली.
एकवीं
Not a word. The first and second of the month use the ordinals पहली and दूसरी.
items.why: The first and second of the month are पहली and दूसरी. After that, the plain number.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Our holiday starts on the fifth of June.”
items.hi: हमारी छुट्टी ___ जून को शुरू होती है ।
items.say: हमारी छुट्टी पाँच जून को शुरू होती है ।
items.en: Our[0] holiday[1] starts[5+6+7] on[4] {the fifth}[2] of June[3].
wrong: पाँचवीं
From the third onwards dates use the plain number: पाँच जून.
पाँचवाँ
From the third onwards dates use the plain number, and पाँचवाँ is masculine anyway.
items.why: तीन मार्च, पाँच जून, but पहली and दूसरी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Yesterday was the second of February.”
items.hi: कल ___ फ़रवरी थी ।
items.say: कल दूसरी फ़रवरी थी ।
wrong: दूसरा
A date agrees with the feminine तारीख़ — दूसरी.
दोवीं
Not a word. “Second” is दूसरी.
items.why: थी agrees with the date, too.

items.q: How is the year 1916 said?
wrong: सन् उन्नीस सौ और सोलह
No word for “and” comes between the hundreds and the rest.
सन् सोलह सौ उन्नीस
That is 1619: the hundreds come first, उन्नीस सौ “nineteen hundred”.
items.why: Years are said in hundreds after सन् “year (of the era)”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “In 2009 we used to live in London.”
items.hi: हम सन् दो ___ नौ में लंदन में रहते थे ।
items.say: हम सन् दो हज़ार नौ में लंदन में रहते थे ।
wrong: सौ
दो सौ नौ is 209.
हज़ारों
हज़ारों is “thousands of”.
items.why: दो हज़ार नौ “two thousand nine”.

items.q: In पहली मई “1st May”, what does पहली agree with?
wrong: The month मई
Masculine months take it too: पहली जून. पहली agrees with the understood तारीख़.
Nothing: पहली never changes
पहला is an ordinary ordinal that agrees; dates take the feminine because of तारीख़.
items.why: पहली तारीख़ “the first date” → पहली.

wrong: रही
रही is feminine. भाई is masculine: धो रहा है.
धोता
धोता है is the imperfective, “washes” as a habit. “Is washing” needs the stem धो + रहा.
रही
रही is feminine. बच्चे is masculine.
था
था is singular. बच्चे is plural: रहे थे.

items.en: Pinki[0] {is writing}[6+7+8] a[4] letter[5] in[3] {her (own)}[1] room[2].
wrong: उसके
उसके would be someone else's room. For the subject's own room, use अपने.
कमरा
Before में the noun is oblique: कमरे.
का
का is masculine. The possessive agrees with बेटियाँ, which is feminine: की.
को
को is for ailments. For relatives, use का, की, के.
नया
नया is masculine. साइकिल is feminine.
को
को is for ailments. A bicycle is a portable thing: के पास.

items.en: My[0] grandmother[1+2] {has had}[3+7] a cold[6] since[5] Monday[4].
wrong: की
Ailments take को — दादी जी को ज़ुकाम है.
The verb agrees with ज़ुकाम, which is singular: है. Respect for दादी जी does not affect it.

items.en: {Next month}[0+1] my[2] uncle[3+4] {is going}[6+7+8] to Calcutta[5].
wrong: अगला
The time phrase is oblique: अगले महीने.
कलकत्तों
Not a word. The destination is oblique singular: कलकत्ते.
इस
इस is oblique, used before a postposition. यह कहानी is the object, with no postposition: यह.
सुनिए
सुनिए is the आप command. This is said to तुम — सुनो.
सवेरा
सवेरा is the noun. As a time phrase it is oblique: सवेरे.
उठता
उठता is singular. बच्चे is plural.

items.en: Our[0] new[1] programme[2] starts[6+7+8] on[5] {the first}[3] of February[4].
wrong: पहला
A date agrees with the feminine तारीख़ — पहली.
एकवीं
Not a word. The first of the month is पहली.
आती
आती is feminine. The English says “he”.
ख़ास
ख़ास तौर पर means “specially”. “Usually” is आम तौर पर.

items.en: {In those days}[0+1] we[2] lived[6+7] in[5] a[3] village[4].
wrong: वे
वे is direct. Before दिनों the phrase is oblique: उन दिनों.
दिन
The phrase is oblique plural: उन दिनों.
के
के अंदर needs a noun before it. On its own, अंदर is an adverb.
बैठो
बैठो is the तुम command. With आप, बैठिए.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरी बहिन अगले महीने भारत आ रही है ।
items.a: My sister is coming to India next month.
wrong: My sister came to India last month.
अगले महीने is “next month”, and आ रही है is not a past tense.
My sister comes to India every month.
A habit would be the imperfective, आती है. Here the continuous tells of a planned event.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे पास थोड़ा-सा समय है ।
wrong: I have no time.
“No time” would need नहीं.
I have a lot of time.
“A lot” would be बहुत. थोड़ा-सा is “a little”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उस समय पिता जी अख़बार पढ़ रहे थे ।
items.a: At that time Father was reading the newspaper.
wrong: At that time Father used to read the newspaper.
“Used to read” would be the past imperfective, पढ़ते थे. पढ़ रहे थे is “was reading”.
Father is reading the newspaper now.
थे puts it in the past, and उस समय is “at that time”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: शर्मा जी की दो बेटियाँ हैं ।
wrong: These are Mr Sharma's two daughters.
“These are” would need ये. With no subject pronoun, X की … हैं means “X has …”.
Mr Sharma has two sons.
बेटियाँ are daughters. Sons would be बेटे, with के.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरा छोटा भाई हमेशा मेरा सिर खाता है ।
items.a: My little brother always pesters me.
wrong: My little brother always eats my food.
सिर is “head”, and सिर खाना is an idiom: “to pester”.
My little brother always hurts my head.
सिर खाना is an idiom meaning “to pester”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: माँ जी आज बीमार दिख रही हैं ।
wrong: Mother is looking at a sick person today.
दिखना means “to appear, seem”. “To look at” is देखना.
Mother was ill today.
दिख रही हैं is present, and it says how she seems.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे पति सावधानी से गाड़ी चलाते हैं ।
wrong: My husband drives fast.
सावधानी से is “with care”, “carefully”.
My husband is driving carefully.
चलाते हैं is the imperfective, a habit. “Is driving” would be चला रहे हैं.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: दूसरे दिन हम काठमांडु में थे ।
items.a: The next day we were in Kathmandu.
wrong: On the second of the month we were in Kathmandu.
A date would be दूसरी, agreeing with तारीख़. दूसरे दिन is “the next day”.
For two days we were in Kathmandu.
“Two days” would be दो दिन. दूसरे दिन is “the next day”.

lessons.title: Rules and usage
lessons.desc: The continuous, “to have”, word order, sounds

items.q: How is the continuous formed?
items.a: Verb stem + रहा, रही or रहे + the auxiliary
wrong: Imperfective participle + रहा + the auxiliary
The participle (बोलता) is not used: it is the bare stem, बोल रहा है.
Infinitive + रहा + the auxiliary
The infinitive (बोलना) is not used: it is the bare stem, बोल रहा है.
items.why: The continuous is the verb stem + रहा, रही or रहे + the auxiliary: बोल रहा है “is speaking”, बोल रहा था “was speaking”.

items.q: Which construction says “X has …” for relatives, houses and parts of the body?
items.a: X का, की, के …, agreeing with what is possessed
wrong: X के पास …
के पास is for portable things, money and time (and servants).
X को …
को is for ailments, as in X को बुख़ार है.
items.why: Hindi has no verb “to have”: it uses होना with को, के पास or का.

items.q: Which is the neutral word order?
items.a: Subject, adverb, indirect object, direct object, verb
wrong: Subject, verb, direct object, indirect object
The verb comes at the end in Hindi.
Direct object, subject, adverb, verb
Putting the object first is possible for effect, but the neutral order starts with the subject.
items.why: The indirect object, with को, comes before the direct object. Changes from this order shift the emphasis.

items.q: Which part is emphasised by its position?
items.a: अपनी बहिन को, just before the verb
wrong: मोहन, the first word
The first place is the normal place for the subject. The position just before the verb often bears emphasis.
किताबें, the direct object
किताबें has moved away from the verb. It is अपनी बहिन को, now just before the verb, that bears the emphasis.
items.why: Neutral order would be मोहन अपनी बहिन को किताबें भेज रहा है.
items.hi: मोहन किताबें अपनी बहिन को भेज रहा है ।
items.say: मोहन किताबें अपनी बहिन को भेज रहा है ।

items.q: What does ऊपर mean with no noun and no के before it?
wrong: It still means “on top of”, with a noun understood
On its own ऊपर has its own adverb sense: मेरा दफ़्तर ऊपर है “my office is upstairs”.
It cannot be used without के
The second part of a compound postposition is often used alone as an adverb.
items.why: के ऊपर “on top of”, ऊपर “up, upstairs”; likewise के नीचे and नीचे.

items.q: Someone says आप बैठो. What is unusual about it?
items.a: It pairs आप with the तुम command form
wrong: Nothing: बैठो is the आप command
The आप command is बैठिए, and बैठो belongs to तुम. The mix is heard as a friendly compromise.
आप is plural, so it should be बैठे
बैठे is not a command. The usual आप command is बैठिए.
items.why: Speakers often mix honorific levels in real speech.

items.q: What does this word mean?
wrong: daal, lentils
That is दाल, with a dental d. डाल has the retroflex ḍ.
political party
That is दल, with a short vowel and a dental d.
items.why: Keep dental and retroflex consonants apart, as in दाल and डाल.
items.hi: डाल

items.q: What does this word mean?
wrong: turn, bend
That is मोड़, with a flapped ṛ at the end.
pearl
That is मोती.
items.why: मोर and मोड़ are a minimal pair.
items.hi: मोर
